text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a burst of port flaps on ToR-17 (eu-west-2 rack 43) starting ~08:12 UTC. We see egress queues spike and a cluster of preemptions on the dedicated-pool for silent-scribe.
liam: on it. is this link-level or BGP? any packet drops?
maria: local logs show LinkDown/LinkUp: "Gi1/0/17 changed state to down" repeatedly. NIC counters on nodes show increasing tx_errors and dropped. no clear BGP churn yet.
josh: rough ps: affected ~6 instances in dedicated-pool-eu, tail latencies spiked ~200ms then preempted. SLO alerts firing.
oncall-bot: [ALERT] egress-queue-latency-p95 exceeded (dedicated-pool-eu) — triggered at 08:16 UTC. Incident channel: #incidents
anya: can we soft-quarantine tenants hitting that ToR? we have soft-quarantine flow (evict traffic to warm-pool/fallback) but not tied to port flap signal.
maria: proposal: add a short-lived port-flap detector -> tag allocations on affected rack with "egress-quarantine" and route to fallback-egress-proxy for 5m. prevents preemptions and noisy tenant cascades.
liam: +1. need to be careful with billing and SLA implications. 5m window seems ok. who owns the routing rule change? netops?
netops: we can add a route-map on ToR to rate-limit egress to the fallback proxy, but it requires change window. if infra can tag allocations we can do it without config change.
maria: infra can tag — we have a scheduler hook. quick plan: 1) detect port-flap via switch syslog -> Kinesis -> infra, 2) infra tags allocations with "egress-quarantine:tor-17", 3) router policy matches tag and reroutes traffic to fallback-egress-proxy. fallback has lower bandwidth but keeps jobs alive.
josh: fallback-egress-proxy capacity? current headroom ~30% in eu-west-2. we should canary before broad rollout.
liam: agree. run canary on 3 non-critical tenants for 10m then scale. also add metrics: preemptions, p95 latency, dropped packets.
anya: small nit: need opt-out for Dedicated customers with strict E2E requirements. tagging must be opt-in/opt-out aware.
maria: yep — only apply to allocations tagged "allow-soft-quarantine=true" by default for bursty tenants. enterprise opt-out respected.
sre-bot: runbook entry updated: "port-flap soft quarantine" added. playbook: detect -> notify netops -> infra-tag -> monitor 10m -> untag.
liam: action items: maria to push detector (lambda + parser), anya to confirm scheduler hook accepts tag, netops to prepare route-map fallback (no change window if infra-based), josh to verify fallback capacity.
maria: I'll open PR with detector parser and test harness. rough CLI to repro:
```
# simulate syslog event
aws kinesis put-record --stream ToR-syslog --data '{"host":"tor-17","msg":"Interface Gi1/0/17 changed state to down"}'
```
liam: please add a metric: `quarantine.applied{tor="tor-17"}` and emit tags so cost dashboard can attribute.
anya: timeline? can we have canary by EOD?
josh: can run canary tonight 22:00 UTC. I'll reserve fallback capacity and watch.
maria: thanks. ping me if anyone sees repeat preemptions after we apply. :thumbsup:
netops: will stand by for verification and won't touch ToR config until we validate infra-only path.
liam: thanks all. I'll update the incident channel and ops board.
maria: closing here, will paste PR link when ready.
